text:
Nashville has won four straight, and the roster that's doing it isn't the one that started the month. The Predators sent Matthew Wood to Seattle for Shane Wright on November 1, Ryan O'Reilly's name keeps surfacing in trade talk, and the team has gone 6-2-2 in its last ten anyway. Steven Stamkos is the face of the run, an overtime winner in Colorado and a goal and an assist against St. Louis, but the engine is the same as it has been for years: Roman Josi and Juuse Saros.

Josi's pairing with Adam Wilsby takes 56% of the expected goals. Saros has been better than his save rate looks, .920 on hard shots and 4.8 goals saved above expected over his last five starts. That matters, because the team in front of him is roughly even: 50% of the expected goals overall and 46% at five on five. Our numbers say Nashville's 21 points are about three more than its play has earned, and the playoff odds sit at 58%.

The best line has been the cheap one. Ross Colton, Jack Drury and Adam Edstrom win 58% of the chances, while the Stamkos and O'Reilly line breaks even. The Brady Skjei and Nick Perbix pairing, at 44%, is the soft spot. If O'Reilly is traded, the question is who centers Stamkos. If he isn't, the question is how long Saros can cover for a 46% team.
